reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 a numeric literal must contain at least one digit, so a sign alone, a decimal point alone, or a sign with a decimal point and no digit must be refused in every numeric-literal position (VALUE, procedure operand, argument list).
reader.edition-search: The rule is a token/grammar shape: INT_BODY [0-9]+ and DEC_BODY ([0-9]+ '.' [0-9]+ | '.' [0-9]+) both require a digit and numericLiteralCore admits only those tokens. Grepped CobolLexer.g4 and CobolExpressions.g4 for predicates on version/edition (none on these rules); LiteralScreen.ScreenDigitCapacity consults EditionInfo.MaxDigits but that is the 18-digit bound, not this rule.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers a bare sign in an ADD operand; the probes add a VALUE clause (VALUE +.), a sign plus decimal point (MOVE -. TO N) and a bare sign in an intrinsic argument list

reader.notes: No token or grammar alternative forms a numeric literal without a digit, at any edition; every digitless form probed at --std 85 is refused, and the one-digit leading-point forms compile and compute correctly.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85: r2a (DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA, VALUE +,) refused COBOL2631/COBOL5506; r2b reference modifier X(+:1) refused COBOL0001; r2c COMPUTE N = . * 2 refused COBOL0001; r2e level-88 VALUE + THRU 5 refused COBOL0001; r2d (class c) 2002 floating-point literal 1.5E3 refused COBOL0900; r2f DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA one-digit leading-comma literals -,5 / ,5 accepted, ADD gives +0,0 +0,0 (algebraically right). No digitless form found that compiles. Check: 'OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.2 SR1 ... the text is in SR1'.
